userStories.title: Objective story pass/fail gate in execution-engine.ts
userStories.description: Prerequisite: rorca-opencode-integration must be complete (OC-004 creates `backend/src/lib/execution-engine.ts`, which replaces both run-loop.sh and run-loop.ts). In `execution-engine.ts`, after the per-story agent subprocess exits with code 0 but BEFORE calling `markStoryPassed()` and `gitCommitStory()`, run an objective validation gate: `npx tsc --noEmit` in the workspace cwd, and `npx playwright test` if a playwright config exists. Use exit codes — not the agent's self-assessment — to determine story outcome. Gate output goes into the WAL event payload.
acceptanceCriteria: In `execution-engine.ts` main story loop, after the agent subprocess exits 0, call a new `runGate(cwd)` function before `markStoryPassed()`
`runGate(cwd)` runs `npx tsc --noEmit` in the workspace cwd; captures stderr
If `playwright.config.ts` or `playwright.config.js` exists in cwd, also runs `npx playwright test --reporter=line`; captures stdout

If tsc exits non-zero, emit `story_failed` WAL event with `{ reason: 'typecheck', stderr: first 2000 chars }` and POST `status: 'fail'` to `/api/pipeline/story-result`; do NOT call `markStoryPassed()`
If playwright exits non-zero, emit `story_failed` with `{ reason: 'e2e', summary: first 2000 chars }`; do NOT call `markStoryPassed()`
If gate passes (both exit 0), proceed to `markStoryPassed()` and `gitCommitStory()` — emit `story_passed`
Gate applies to all three agent paths (claude, opencode, codex) — it runs in execution-engine.ts regardless of agent type
Gate is skipped when `--dry-run` flag is set or `RORCA_SKIP_GATE=1` env var is present
Gate timeout: 5 minutes max (separate from the story execution timeout)

userStories.title: Quick run backend — auto-generate and auto-approve a 1-story micro-spec
userStories.description: Add `POST /api/pipeline/quick-run` that accepts a plain-English brief and a workspace ID. It calls the spec generator with a constraint to produce exactly 1 user story, writes the spec directly to `ralph/specs/approved/` (skipping the review queue), inserts a `spec_approved` WAL event with `actor: 'quick-run'`, then immediately triggers the execution engine (execution-engine.ts when opencode-integration is complete, run-loop.ts otherwise). Returns `{ runId, specId }`. The spec file and WAL record are preserved exactly as for normal runs — no auditability is lost.
acceptanceCriteria: `POST /api/pipeline/quick-run` accepts `{ workspaceId, brief, model? }` body
LLM prompt constrains output to exactly 1 user story with ≤5 acceptance criteria
Spec is written to `ralph/specs/approved/<slug>.json` — never to `pending/`
A `spec_approved` WAL event is written with `actor: 'quick-run'`
Pipeline is triggered immediately — no manual approval step
Returns `{ runId, specId }` with HTTP 202
Conflict detection still applies — returns `{ conflict: true, activeRunId }` if workspace has an active run
Quick-run specs are distinguishable in the Archive by a `source: 'quick-run'` tag on the spec

userStories.title: Semantic log parser — extract structured steps from stream-json and OpenCode JSON output
userStories.description: Build `backend/src/lib/semantic-log-parser.ts` that parses the already-structured JSON output from both execution paths into `SemanticStep` objects. The claude path uses `--output-format stream-json` — each log line is a JSON object with a `type` field (e.g. `tool_use`, `tool_result`, `assistant`, `result`). The OpenCode path uses `--format json` with its own event schema. No regex needed for either path. The parser tails the run's log file (same file used by the xterm SSE stream) and emits `semantic_step` SSE events on `GET /api/pipeline/runs/:id/output` alongside the existing raw byte events.
acceptanceCriteria: `semantic-log-parser.ts` exports `parseStreamJsonLine(line: string): SemanticStep | null` for claude `--output-format stream-json` log lines
`semantic-log-parser.ts` exports `parseOpenCodeLine(line: string): SemanticStep | null` for OpenCode `--format json` log lines
`SemanticStep` type: `{ type: 'read' | 'write' | 'edit' | 'bash' | 'plan' | 'commit' | 'test' | 'search' | 'unknown', label: string, detail?: string, ts: string }`
For claude stream-json: `tool_use` events with `name: 'Read'` → type `read`, `name: 'Edit'` → `edit`, `name: 'Bash'` → `bash`, `name: 'Write'` → `write`, `name: 'Glob'/'Grep'` → `search`
For claude stream-json: `result` event with `subtype: 'success'` → type `commit` with label from last git commit message if present in output

The existing log-tailing loop in the pipeline SSE endpoint calls the parser on each line and emits `event: semantic_step
data: <json>

` alongside raw bytes
Execution path (claude vs opencode) is detected from the `pipeline_runs` record's `agent` column
Parser never throws — malformed or non-semantic lines return null
Unit tests cover at least 8 representative line formats from each path

userStories.title: Semantic log UI — toggle between raw terminal and structured step view in RunTerminal

acceptanceCriteria: A Raw / Semantic toggle button appears in the RunTerminal toolbar
In Semantic mode, xterm is hidden and a step list is rendered
Each step shows: step-type icon, label, relative timestamp
Steps with a `detail` field show a expand/collapse chevron
New steps auto-append and the list auto-scrolls to bottom
In Raw mode, xterm renders as before — no regression
Toggle state is saved to localStorage keyed by runId
If no semantic events have arrived yet (e.g. old run), Semantic mode shows 'No semantic data available for this run' and falls back gracefully

userStories.title: Inline story editing in the Review Queue before approval
userStories.description: In ReviewQueuePanel, clicking a story card should expand an editable view (using the existing InlineStoryEditor component) that allows editing the story title, description, and acceptance criteria before the spec is approved. Saves are written back to the spec JSON file on disk and create a new entry in `spec_versions`. The approve/reject decision is unchanged — this is purely a pre-approval editing step. A 'modified' badge appears on edited stories.
acceptanceCriteria: Clicking a story card in ReviewQueuePanel expands an inline editor (title, description, acceptance criteria list)
Editing and saving calls `PATCH /api/specs/:id/stories/:storyId` which updates the spec JSON on disk
On save, a new `spec_versions` record is written
A 'Modified' badge appears on the story card if any field differs from the last approved/generated version
Approve/reject buttons remain unchanged and operate on the current (edited) version
Unsaved changes show a confirmation prompt if the user navigates away or approves without saving
`PATCH /api/specs/:id/stories/:storyId` validates that the spec is in `pending/` — editing approved specs is not allowed via this endpoint

userStories.title: Shareable read-only spec review link
userStories.description: Add a 'Share for Review' button in ReviewQueuePanel that generates a signed token and returns a URL like `http://localhost:5210/review/:token`. The `/review/:token` route renders a read-only view of the spec with all stories and acceptance criteria, plus a comment box per story (using the existing `story_comments` table). Comments are attributed to 'Guest' or a name the reviewer types. The spec owner sees new comments in the Review Queue. This enables async stakeholder review before a single line of code runs.

Returns `{ url: 'http://localhost:5210/review/:token' }` — URL uses the current frontend origin from env
`GET /api/review/:token` (public, no auth) returns spec stories + existing comments for that spec
`POST /api/review/:token/comments` (public) accepts `{ storyId, body, authorName }` — writes to `story_comments` with `user_id: null` and `author_name` field
Frontend `/review/:token` route renders the spec title, story list with acceptance criteria, and comment threads per story
Reviewer can add a name before commenting (stored in localStorage for the session)
ReviewQueuePanel shows a comment count badge on stories that have comments, and a notification dot on the 'Share for Review' button when new comments have arrived since last viewed
Expired or invalid tokens return a clear error page

userStories.title: Wave compiler — dependency DAG topological sort into parallel execution groups
userStories.description: Build `backend/src/lib/wave-compiler.ts` that takes a spec's `userStories` array and compiles it into an ordered array of waves using Kahn's algorithm. Each wave is a set of stories whose `dependsOn` dependencies all appear in earlier waves — meaning they can be executed concurrently without ordering violations. This module is execution-engine-agnostic: it is called by both `run-loop.ts` (current) and `execution-engine.ts` (after opencode-integration ships). The `parallelGroups` helper already exists in `backend/src/routes/specs.ts` for the graph API — extract and generalise it into this standalone module. Stories with `passes: true` are excluded from compilation (already done). Cycle detection returns a typed error.
acceptanceCriteria: `backend/src/lib/wave-compiler.ts` exports `compileWaves(stories: UserStory[]): Wave[] | CycleError`
`Wave` type: `{ index: number, stories: UserStory[] }` — index 0 is the first wave
Kahn's algorithm: initialise in-degree map, enqueue zero-in-degree nodes, drain per wave level
Stories with `passes: true` are excluded before compilation — waves are built from pending stories only
Cycle detection: if any stories remain after Kahn's drains (in-degree never reached 0), return `{ cycle: true, involvedIds: string[] }`
Single-story and zero-dependency specs produce a single wave containing all stories
Stories with `dependsOn` referencing already-passed story IDs treat those deps as satisfied
Unit tests cover: linear chain (each story depends on previous), diamond DAG, fully independent (all in wave 0), cycle detection, mixed passed/pending
The existing `computeParallelGroups` helper in `specs.ts` is replaced with a call to `compileWaves` from this module to eliminate duplication

userStories.title: Parallel worker pool — concurrent story subprocess execution per wave
userStories.description: Extend `backend/src/lib/run-loop.ts` (and `execution-engine.ts` once it exists) to accept a `--parallelism N` flag (1–10, default 1). When N > 1, use the wave compiler output (EQ-008) to fan out: for each wave, spawn up to N concurrent story subprocesses using `Promise.allSettled`. A story that fails marks all stories in subsequent waves that transitively depend on it as `blocked` — not failed — and they are skipped cleanly. Sequential (N=1) behaviour is identical to today: stories run one-by-one in wave order. The parallelism value is stored on the `pipeline_runs` row so the UI can display it.
acceptanceCriteria: `run-loop.ts` accepts `--parallelism <N>` flag; N is parsed as integer, clamped to 1–10, default 1
When N=1, execution is identical to existing sequential behaviour — no regression
When N>1, `compileWaves()` is called and stories within each wave are spawned concurrently up to N processes
`Promise.allSettled` used per wave so a single story failure does not kill sibling stories mid-wave

After each wave settles: check for failed stories, compute which subsequent stories are transitively blocked, emit `story_failed` WAL events for blocked stories with `{ reason: 'blocked_by', blockedBy: string[] }`
Proceed to next wave only after all stories in current wave have settled (passed, failed, or skipped)
Each parallel story subprocess receives its own `--story <ID>` flag and its own worktree path (from EQ-010)
`pipeline_runs.parallelism` column (integer, default 1) stores the configured value — add via `pragma table_info` check in `db/index.ts`
WAL `run_started` event payload includes `{ parallelism: N, waveCount: number }` fields
Concurrency is bounded: if wave has 10 stories and N=3, only 3 run at once — remaining queue as workers free up

When `RORCA_AGENT=opencode` and parallelism > 1: omit the `--attach` flag so each story spawns its own isolated OpenCode server instance — parallelism safety takes priority over warm-server performance. When parallelism=1 (sequential), `--attach` is retained as normal for the warm-server benefit.

userStories.title: Per-story auto-worktree isolation for parallel runs
userStories.description: When parallelism > 1, each story in a wave must execute in its own isolated git worktree to prevent concurrent file system conflicts. Before spawning each story subprocess, create a worktree branch `feat/<specSlug>-<storyId>-<ts>` in a sibling directory. After the story subprocess exits (pass or fail), merge the worktree back to the parent branch (on pass) or discard it (on fail). Sequential runs (parallelism=1) are unaffected — worktrees only when explicitly running in parallel. Worktree paths are stored in `story_results` for traceability.
acceptanceCriteria: When parallelism > 1: before spawning story subprocess, call `git worktree add -b feat/<specSlug>-<storyId>-<ts> <worktreePath> HEAD`
Worktree path: `path.resolve(workspace.path, '..', '<repoName>-<storyId>-<ts>')` — sibling of the main workspace
Story subprocess receives the worktree path as its `--cwd` argument, not the main workspace path
On story pass: merge worktree branch back to the wave's merge target (main workspace branch) after the full wave settles — not immediately after story exits
On story fail: `git worktree remove --force <worktreePath>` — no merge, no leftover branch
`story_results` table: add `worktree_path` and `worktree_branch` columns (via `pragma table_info` guard in `db/index.ts`)
Worktree creation failure (e.g. disk full) is treated as a story failure with `{ reason: 'worktree_create_failed' }` WAL event
Sequential runs (parallelism=1) create no extra worktrees — existing `autoWorktree` flag behaviour unchanged
After successful merge, worktree and branch are deleted: `git worktree remove` + `git branch -d`

userStories.title: Wave merge orchestrator — sequential merge after each wave with conflict resolution
userStories.description: After all stories in a wave pass (EQ-010 created per-story worktrees), the wave merge orchestrator merges each worktree branch into the parent branch sequentially in deterministic story-ID order. It uses `git merge --no-ff --no-commit` first to detect conflicts before committing. On a clean merge it commits. On a conflict it attempts auto-resolution: run `git diff --name-only --diff-filter=U` to get conflicting files, then spawn a single short Claude invocation (`claude --print`) with the conflict diffs asking it to produce the resolved content. If auto-resolution fails, emit a `run_blocked` WAL event listing conflicting files and pause the run until the user resolves manually via HITL.
acceptanceCriteria: After a wave's `Promise.allSettled` resolves with all-pass, call `mergeWave(waveBranches: string[], targetBranch: string, cwd: string)`
Merges are sequential in ascending story-ID order for determinism
Each merge: `git merge --no-ff --no-commit <branch>` — on exit 0 run `git commit -m 'merge: <storyId>'`
On merge conflict: run `git diff --name-only --diff-filter=U` to list conflicting files

Auto-resolution attempt: for each conflicting file, read the conflict markers and call `claude --print` with a structured prompt: 'Resolve this git merge conflict. Output only the resolved file content.' — write result back to file, `git add <file>`
If all conflicts resolved: `git commit -m 'merge(wave-N): resolved conflicts in <files>'`
If auto-resolution fails or Claude exits non-zero: `git merge --abort`, emit `run_blocked` WAL event with `{ reason: 'merge_conflict', conflictingFiles: string[], wave: number }`, pause the run
After wave merge completes successfully: delete all worktrees and branches from the wave
WAL event `wave_merged` emitted after each successful wave merge with `{ wave: number, storiesCount: number, conflictsResolved: number }`
If a wave has only 1 story (sequential case), skip the merge orchestrator — the story already committed directly

userStories.title: Parallelism parameter in pipeline trigger API and trigger UI

Validation: non-integer, out-of-range, or negative values return HTTP 400 with descriptive error
`--parallelism <N>` flag appended to the run-loop spawn arguments when N > 1
Hub Ready-to-Run trigger button opens a small popover with: parallelism stepper (1–10 with +/- buttons), 'Use worktrees' checkbox (auto-checked when N > 1), and a 'Trigger' confirm button
Archive panel trigger button uses the same popover component
Default parallelism pre-filled from workspace settings (new `default_parallelism` column in `workspaces` table, default 1)

userStories.title: Wave progress UI — grouped story list with per-wave status in Run View
userStories.description: When a run uses parallelism > 1, the Run View story list groups stories by wave. Each wave has a collapsible header showing wave index, story count, and aggregate status. Stories within a wave are shown with independent per-story progress (elapsed time, status icon). The wave header shows a fan-out animation when the wave starts and a fan-in merge indicator while the wave merge orchestrator runs. Sequential runs (parallelism=1) show the existing flat story list unchanged.
acceptanceCriteria: Run View detects `parallelism > 1` from the `pipeline_runs` record and switches story list to wave-grouped layout
Wave header: 'Wave N — M stories' with aggregate status chip (waiting/running/merging/done/partial-fail)
Wave header is collapsible — expanded by default for the active wave, collapsed for completed waves
Stories within a wave show side-by-side or as indented sub-list (design choice: indented sub-list is simpler, preferred)
Each story row in a wave shows: status icon, title, elapsed time (counting up while running)
When wave starts: wave header animates from 'waiting' to 'running' with a brief pulse
When all wave stories settle and merge begins: wave header shows 'Merging...' spinner
After merge: wave header shows 'Done' (all pass) or 'Partial fail' (some failed) with story count breakdown
WAL events `wave_merged` and `story_failed` with `reason: 'blocked_by'` drive the wave status updates via existing SSE
Sequential run (parallelism=1): existing flat story list unchanged — no wave headers shown

userStories.title: Rate limit backpressure and transparent retry queue
userStories.description: When Claude's subscription rate limit is hit during a parallel run, the affected story subprocess exits with a detectable error rather than being counted as a story failure. The worker pool catches this, parks the story in a retry queue with exponential backoff, and re-spawns it when the backoff timer expires — transparently, without user intervention. Rate limit retries do not count against `MAX_RETRIES`. The UI shows affected stories in an amber 'Rate limited — retry in Xs' state with a live countdown.
acceptanceCriteria: Rate limit detection in story subprocess wrapper: stderr contains 'rate limit exceeded' or 'overloaded' (case-insensitive), OR process exits with code 1 within < 5 seconds of start (heuristic for immediate rejection)
On rate limit detection: do NOT call `markStoryFailed()` — instead emit WAL `story_rate_limited` event with `{ attempt: number, retryAfterMs: number }`
Exponential backoff schedule: attempt 1 → 30s, attempt 2 → 60s, attempt 3 → 120s, attempt 4 → 240s. After 4 rate-limit attempts, mark story failed with `{ reason: 'rate_limit_exhausted' }`
Rate limit retries are tracked separately from `MAX_RETRIES` (story logic errors) — both limits apply independently
During backoff: story slot in the wave is parked — other stories in the wave continue running; the wave does not wait for the parked story before starting
After backoff timer expires: re-spawn the story subprocess in the same worktree
WAL `story_rate_limited` payload includes `{ storyId, attempt, retryAfterMs, waveIndex }` — visible in activity feed
Run View UI: rate-limited story row shows amber background, clock icon, 'Rate limited — retry in Xs' with live countdown using SSE-driven state
Countdown updates every second via a client-side timer seeded from the `retryAfterMs` in the WAL event — no additional SSE events needed for the tick
On successful retry: story resumes normal pass/fail flow — row transitions from amber to blue (running) to green (passed)
